## 0. Conventions, imported inputs, and what is proved where

Throughout k is a field of characteristic zero and all stacks are algebraic k-stacks. For a triple (pi:C->T, sigma:P->T, gamma:C->P) as in the theorem write p:=pi, and set

- E := (coker(O_P -> gamma_*O_C))^vee, locally free of rank 3;
- O_P(1) := det(E) tensor omega_{P/T}^{tensor 4};
- D := gamma^*O_P(1), Lbar := omega_{C/T} tensor gamma^*O_P(-1).

On a geometric fibre, gamma_*O_C = O direct-sum E^vee with E^vee = direct-sum_i O(-e_i); since C_b is proper connected, h^0(E^vee)=h^0(O_{C_b})-1=0, so e_i>=1, and chi(O_{C_b})=1-g gives sum_i e_i = g+d-1 = 9, i.e. deg E = 9. Hence deg O_P(1) = 9 + 4(-2) = 1 on every geometric fibre, so O_P(1) is a canonically defined relative-degree-one line bundle: no choice, no Brauer obstruction, and P = P((sigma_*O_P(1))^vee). Also deg D = 4 and deg Lbar = (2g-2) - 4 = 6.

**Source-backed input (not proved here).** (CE): the relative Casnati-Ekedahl structure recorded in SRC-0004 (Lemma 10.6 and the degree-four structure theorem): the P-embedding i:C->X=P(E^vee) with p o i = gamma, the relative resolution 0->O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F->O_X(-2) tensor p^*F->I_C->0 and p_*O_X(m)=Sym^m E. From the resolution, twisting by O_X(2) and using R^j p_* O_X(-2)=0 for all j on a P^2-bundle, one gets F = p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)) and the exact sequence 0->F->Sym^2 E->gamma_*(i^*O_X(2))->0; so F is intrinsic to (C,P,gamma), is locally free of rank 2 with fibre degree 9, and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change.

**Verified dependency artifacts.** ATT-0065 (dual-confirmed by REV-0108, REV-0109): CLM-0065-5 constructs the canonical maximal-degree line subbundle of a fibrewise balanced F and the induced filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 with fibre degrees 20 and 16; CLM-0065-9 identifies the balanced ambient CE evaluation-failure scheme with the relative incidence O_C(Gamma) iso W_5 tensor omega^{-1}. ATT-0066 (dual-confirmed by REV-0110, REV-0116): CLM-0066-5 supplies the base-independent Abel-Jacobi/Hilbert incidence model, CLM-0066-4 the projective-bundle model on a reduced constant-h^0 stratum, CLM-0066-6 the stack-level ordered S_6-torsor. Supporting context: ATT-0086 (REV-0135, REV-0138) proves that the h^0(L)=4 stratum is empty on the balanced locus; ATT-0088 (REV-0139, REV-0142) records, under (CE)+(BAL)+(N), non-hyperellipticity, h^0(L)=3 and nonemptiness of the reduced-support locus. I re-prove below the facts I actually use, in the normalization-free form needed for Lbar, but I do not claim novelty for the reduced-member statement, which ATT-0088 already contains.

**Established working-context facts used verbatim.** (i) A hyperelliptic genus-6 degree-four cover has E=O(1)+O(4)^2 and cannot have balanced F (equivalently h^0(F(-6))>=2>0). (ii) For every degree-four cover of a genus-6 curve, h^0(O_C(D)) is 2 or 3, and equals 3 exactly in the hyperelliptic-composed case. (iii) Irreducible components of a Zariski-locally trivial projective bundle correspond bijectively to those of the base. (iv) Ordering the six points over the distinct-support locus is a finite etale S_6-torsor at stack level.

Status separation is collected in Section 8.

## 1. The tetragonal stack is smooth Deligne-Mumford of pure dimension 15

### 1.1 Algebraicity, finite type, Deligne-Mumford

A triple is the same datum as a genus-0 fibration P->T together with a finite locally free O_P-algebra A of rank 4 such that C=Spec_P(A) is smooth and proper over T with geometrically connected genus-6 fibres. The stack of genus-0 fibrations is B PGL_2, algebraic and smooth of dimension -3; the stack of finite locally free rank-4 algebras over the universal genus-0 fibration is algebraic (algebra structures on a rank-4 bundle form a closed subscheme of a vector bundle of multiplication maps, and the underlying bundles are parametrized by a smooth algebraic stack); smoothness of C/T, geometric connectedness and the genus condition are open conditions. Hence Tet is algebraic. It is of finite type because the fibrewise splitting type of gamma_*O_C = O + direct-sum_i O(-e_i) is constrained by e_i>=1 and sum e_i=9 (Section 0), so only finitely many splitting types occur and the family is bounded. Automorphisms of an object over an algebraically closed field are pairs (s,t) with s in Aut(C), t in Aut(P) and t o gamma = gamma o s; since gamma is surjective, t is determined by s, and Aut(C) is finite for g=6>=2, so all automorphism groups are finite and Tet is Deligne-Mumford.

### 1.2 Deformations of a degree-four cover with fixed target

Fix a geometric point and first fix the target: let Cov denote the stack of pairs (C,gamma:C->Y) with Y=P^1_k fixed. Deformations of a scheme over a fixed base Y are controlled by the cotangent complex L_{C/Y}: the tangent space is Ext^1_{O_C}(L_{C/Y},O_C) and obstructions lie in Ext^2_{O_C}(L_{C/Y},O_C). Since C and Y are smooth over k, the transitivity triangle gives L_{C/Y} = cone(gamma^*Omega_Y -> Omega_C). In characteristic zero gamma is generically etale, so gamma^*Omega_Y -> Omega_C is a nonzero map of invertible sheaves, hence injective, hence

  L_{C/Y} quasi-isomorphic to Omega_{C/Y},

a torsion sheaf whose length is deg(Omega_C) - deg(gamma^*Omega_Y) = (2g-2) + 2d = 10 + 8 = 18 (Riemann-Hurwitz). This length computation is insensitive to the ramification profile: it counts the ramification divisor with multiplicity, not distinct branch points.

For a torsion sheaf tau on a smooth curve, Hom(tau,O_C)=0, the sheaf Ext^1(tau,O_C) is torsion of the same length, and Ext^q(tau,O_C)=0 for q>=2 because O_C has injective dimension 1. The local-to-global spectral sequence gives

  Ext^1(Omega_{C/Y},O_C) = H^0(Ext^1(Omega_{C/Y},O_C)), of dimension 18,
  Ext^2(Omega_{C/Y},O_C) = H^1(Ext^1(Omega_{C/Y},O_C)) = 0,

since H^1 of a torsion sheaf on a curve vanishes. Deformations are therefore unobstructed and the deformation space has dimension 18 at every point. Flatness, finiteness, smoothness of the source and geometric connectedness are open, so all nearby deformations are again objects of Cov. Hence Cov is smooth of pure dimension 18.

### 1.3 Descent of the target

The morphism Tet -> B PGL_2 sending (C,P,gamma) to P has the property that its base change along the smooth surjective atlas Spec k -> B PGL_2 (a PGL_2-torsor, relative dimension 3) is Cov. Thus Cov -> Tet is smooth surjective of relative dimension 3. Smoothness descends along smooth surjections and dimensions subtract, so Tet is smooth of pure dimension 18 - 3 = 15. This proves clause (A) except for openness and nonemptiness of Bal.

Remark on a recorded dead route: the dimension is obtained here from the length-18 torsion sheaf Omega_{C/P} and not from a count of distinct branch points, so the objection that collisions and higher ramification change the branch-point count does not apply.

## 2. Balancedness is open, and Bal is nonempty

### 2.1 Openness

On a geometric fibre F_b is a rank-2 bundle of degree 9 on P^1, so F_b = O(a) + O(9-a) with a <= 4, and

  h^0(F_b tensor omega_{P_b}^{tensor 3}) = h^0(F_b(-6)) = h^0(O(a-6)) + h^0(O(3-a)) = 4-a for a <= 4.

Thus the vanishing of h^0(F_b(-6)) is equivalent to a = 4, i.e. to F_b = O(4)+O(5). Since F is locally free on P and omega_{P/T} is defined without any choice, semicontinuity of h^0 along the proper morphism sigma shows Bal is open in Tet. Being a nonempty open substack of a smooth stack of pure dimension 15, Bal is smooth of pure dimension 15, hence reduced and normal, and a connected normal locally Noetherian stack is irreducible, so its connected components are its irreducible components.

### 2.2 An explicit balanced point (existence, not a universal claim)

Let C be a smooth complete intersection of divisors of bidegrees (1,2) and (2,2) in P^1 x P^2, and gamma := pr_1. Both linear systems are base-point-free and ample, so a general such C is smooth (Bertini) and connected (an ample divisor on the smooth ample surface cut by the first equation; Kodaira vanishing gives h^0(O_C)=1). Adjunction: omega_C = O_C(-2,-3) tensor O_C(3,4) = O_C(1,1). With [C] = (H_1+2H_2)(2H_1+2H_2) = 6H_1H_2 + 4H_2^2 one gets [C].H_1 = 4 and [C].H_2 = 6, so deg omega_C = 10 and g(C)=6, and gamma has degree 4. All fibres are finite (C is irreducible and dominates P^1), and gamma is flat by miracle flatness. So (C,P^1,gamma) is an object of Tet.

Compute the invariants directly from the Koszul resolution 0->O(-3,-4)->O(-1,-2) direct-sum O(-2,-2)->O->O_C->0.

- Pushing along q=pr_1: Rq_*O(-1,-2)=Rq_*O(-2,-2)=0 and Rq_*O(-3,-4)=O(-3)^3[-2] (h^2(P^2,O(-4))=3), so gamma_*O_C = O direct-sum O(-3)^3 and E = O(3)^3, deg E = 9 as required.
- Hence X = P(E^vee) = P^1 x P^2 with p_*O_X(1) = E = O(3)^3, i.e. O_X(1)=O(3,1). Check: deg(O_X(1)|_C) = 3.4 + 1.6 = 18 = 2g-2+4.2, matching SRC-0004.
- The Koszul resolution has exactly the CE shape: O_X(-2) tensor p^*F = O(-6,-2) tensor p^*F equals O(-1,-2) direct-sum O(-2,-2) precisely for F = O(5) direct-sum O(4), and then O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F = O(-12,-4) tensor O(9) = O(-3,-4), which is the third Koszul term. Independently and without matching conventions, F = p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)): twisting the Koszul resolution by O(6,2) gives 0->O(3,-2)->O(5,0) direct-sum O(4,0)->I_C(2)->0 and Rq_*O(3,-2)=0, so p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)) = O(4) direct-sum O(5). Hence C is balanced and Bal is nonempty.
- Moreover i^*O_X(1) = O_C(3,1) = O_C(1,1) tensor O_C(2,0) = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2) = omega_{C/P^1}, so the weak normalization (N) holds here with A = O; O_P(1) = det E tensor omega^{4} = O(9-8)=O(1); D = gamma^*O(1) = O_C(1,0); Lbar = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(-1) = O_C(0,1), of degree 6; and W_5 = i^*O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-5) = O_C(6,2) tensor O_C(-5,0) = O_C(1,2), so W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = O_C(0,1) = Lbar, as clause (F) predicts.
- Finally h^0(C,O_C(0,1)) = 3: twisting the Koszul resolution by O(0,1) gives H^0 = 3 and H^0 = H^1 = 0 for both O(-1,-1) and O(-2,-1). The system |O_C(0,1)| is the pullback of the lines of P^2, hence base-point-free, so by Bertini in characteristic zero its general member is a reduced divisor of six distinct points. Thus the ordered model Z is nonempty.

This is a single explicit object; it is used only for existence statements (Bal and Z are nonempty), never for a universal claim.

## 3. Fibrewise numerics on Bal (no normalization used)

Let b be a geometric point of Bal, C=C_b, gamma=gamma_b, D = gamma^*O(1) of degree 4, Lbar = omega_C(-D) of degree 6.

(3.1) h^0(D)=2. Pullback of the pencil gives h^0(D)>=2; Riemann-Roch gives h^0(D)-h^1(D) = 4-6+1 = -1, so h^1(D)=h^0(D)+1>0 and D is special; Clifford gives h^0(D) <= deg(D)/2+1 = 3, with equality only if D is O_C, omega_C, or C is hyperelliptic with D linearly equivalent to twice the g^1_2. Since deg D = 4 is neither 0 nor 2g-2 = 10, equality forces C hyperelliptic; but a hyperelliptic genus-6 degree-four cover has E = O(1)+O(4)^2 and h^0(F(-6))>=2, contradicting balancedness. Hence h^0(D)=2 on Bal.

(3.2) chi(Lbar)=6-6+1=1 and h^1(Lbar)=h^0(omega_C tensor Lbar^{-1})=h^0(D)=2, so h^0(Lbar)=3 and h^1(Lbar)=2 on every geometric point of Bal. In particular the h^0-value is constant: there is no jump stratum to stratify over. (This is the normalization-free analogue of the emptiness of B_4 proved in ATT-0086/CLM-0086-1 and used in ATT-0088.)

(3.3) |Lbar| contains a reduced divisor. If some point q had multiplicity at least two in the fixed part, then h^0(Lbar(-2q)) = 3 with deg(Lbar(-2q)) = 4; this bundle is special because h^1(Lbar(-2q)) = h^0(D+2q) >= h^0(D) = 2 > 0; Clifford then gives 3 <= 4/2+1 = 3, an equality case with degree 4 not in {0,10}, hence C hyperelliptic, hence unbalanced: contradiction. So the fixed part Phi of |Lbar| is reduced. Its moving part is base-point-free of projective dimension 2, so by Bertini a general member of the moving part is reduced, and for each of the finitely many points of Supp(Phi) the sections vanishing there form a hyperplane, so a general member of the moving part avoids Supp(Phi). A general member of |Lbar| is therefore Phi plus a reduced divisor disjoint from it, hence reduced, hence six distinct points. (Statement already contained in ATT-0088; the proof above is independent and normalization-free.)

## 4. The P^2-bundle over the universal base, and arbitrary (possibly nonreduced) bases

(4.1) Over Bal itself. Bal is smooth over k, hence reduced, and h^0(Lbar_b)=3 is constant by (3.2). Grauert's theorem applies on any smooth atlas U->Bal (U a smooth, hence reduced, scheme; flat base change identifies the pushforward on U with the pullback of the one on Bal, and local freeness is smooth-local), so p_*Lbar is locally free of rank 3. Since the base-change map (p_*Lbar) tensor k(s) -> H^0(Lbar_s) is surjective at every point, cohomology and base change gives that the formation of p_*Lbar commutes with arbitrary base change, including nonreduced ones. By ATT-0066/CLM-0066-4 and FND-0107, over a base with p_*Lbar locally free and base-change compatible, the Abel-Jacobi incidence I = Sym^6 x_{Pic^6} Bal represents relative effective divisors Gamma with O(Gamma) iso Lbar tensor (pullback from the base) and is canonically P((p_*Lbar)^vee); projectivization of a locally free rank-3 sheaf is Zariski-locally trivial, so I->Bal is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle, smooth and proper of pure relative dimension 2. With (A), dim I = 17, pure.

(4.2) Arbitrary bases. Let T be any locally Noetherian k-scheme (or locally Noetherian algebraic k-stack with a smooth atlas) carrying a family of triples satisfying (CE) and fibrewise balancedness. By the moduli property of Bal the family is classified by a 1-morphism psi:T->Bal, and all the data are pullbacks along psi: this includes E, O_P(1), D and Lbar, which are formed by universal constructions commuting with base change. Formation of Sym^6(C/T) and of the relative Picard functor commutes with base change, so the incidence for T is I x_{Bal} T; and since p_*Lbar commutes with arbitrary base change by (4.1), p_{T*}Lbar_T = psi^*(p_*Lbar) is locally free of rank 3 and I_T = P((p_{T*}Lbar_T)^vee) is again a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle. No reducedness of T is used anywhere: Grauert is applied only on the smooth universal base, and the transport is by flat/arbitrary base change. This is the extension flagged as not carried out (nonreduced bases, stack bases with a smooth atlas); it does not contradict FND-0131, which correctly says that constant fibre dimensions alone do not suffice over a nonreduced base -- the extra input here is smoothness of the universal balanced base, proved in Section 1. The stack-base clause carries the descent remark demanded by FND-0127: Grauert local freeness with base change is smooth-local on the base, reducedness is preserved by smooth pullback in characteristic zero, and the identification of the Abel-Jacobi incidence with P((p_*Lbar)^vee) is canonical (given by the universal divisor), hence descends along a smooth atlas.

## 5. Distinct-support open, the S_6-torsor, and components

By (3.3) the fibre of I^dist over every geometric point of Bal is a nonempty open subset of the irreducible fibre |Lbar_b| = P^2; hence I^dist -> Bal is surjective and smooth with irreducible two-dimensional fibres, and I^dist is a dense open substack of I. Ordering the six pairwise-distinct points is a free S_6-action, and Z = Conf_6(C/Bal) x_{Sym^6} I -> I^dist is a finite etale S_6-torsor at stack level (established fact; ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6). Reduction is applied to neither side: both source and target keep their scheme structures, so the recorded one-sided-reduction failure is avoided.

Since I is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle over the smooth Bal and Z is finite etale over the open I^dist of I, both I and Z are smooth over k, hence normal, hence their connected components are irreducible. dim Z = dim I^dist = dim I = 17, pure, and Z is nonempty by Section 2.2.

Component correspondence. For a component Bal_alpha (irreducible by (A)), I_alpha is irreducible (locally trivial bundle with irreducible fibre over an irreducible base), and I^dist_alpha is a nonempty open in I_alpha, hence irreducible and dense. Therefore {components of I^dist} -> {components of I} -> {components of Bal} are bijections. For the torsor, the fibre over a geometric base point of I^dist_alpha is a principal homogeneous S_6-set, and its connected components correspond to the orbits of the etale monodromy image H_alpha acting by translation, i.e. to the coset space H_alpha \ S_6; by normality of Z these connected components are exactly the irreducible components, so Z has precisely [S_6:H_alpha] irreducible components over Bal_alpha, each of dimension 17. The normality hypothesis that FND-0132 requires for this upgrade is here supplied by the smoothness proved in Section 1, not assumed; the subgroups H_alpha themselves remain undetermined (Section 8).

## 6. The morphism to M_{6,6}: full faithfulness, unramifiedness, quasi-finiteness, inertia, codimension

An object of Z over T is (C,P,gamma,x_1,...,x_6) with x_i pairwise disjoint sections of the smooth proper genus-6 curve C/T and Gamma = sum x_i satisfying O_C(Gamma) iso Lbar tensor pi^*M for some line bundle M on T. Since 2g-2+n = 16 > 0, (C,x_1,...,x_6) is an object of M_{6,6}(T); this defines Theta.

### 6.1 Functorial reconstruction of (P,gamma) from (C,Gamma)

On Z we have, canonically,

  omega_{C/T}(-Gamma) iso omega_{C/T} tensor Lbar^{-1} tensor pi^*M^{-1} = gamma^*O_P(1) tensor pi^*M^{-1}.   (6.1)

Put V := p_*(omega_{C/T}(-Gamma)). By (6.1) and the projection formula, V = sigma_*(O_P(1)) tensor M^{-1} direct-sum sigma_*(E^vee tensor O_P(1)) tensor M^{-1}.

- sigma_*O_P(1) is locally free of rank 2 and commutes with arbitrary base change, because O_P(1) has fibre degree 1 on a genus-0 fibration, so R^1 sigma_* O_P(1) = 0 fibrewise and cohomology and base change applies. No reducedness is used.
- sigma_*(E^vee tensor O_P(1)) = 0 over an arbitrary base. Fibrewise h^0(E^vee(1)) = #{i : e_i = 1} = h^0(D) - 2 = 0 by (3.1). Represent R sigma_*(E^vee(1)) by a two-term complex of bundles d:K^0->K^1; vanishing of H^0 on every fibre means d tensor k(t) is injective for every t, i.e. d has constant maximal rank, so the corresponding minor ideal is the unit ideal and d is locally a split injection; hence ker d = 0 and sigma_*(E^vee(1)) = 0. Constant maximal rank does give local splitting even over nonreduced bases, so this step is legitimate over any locally Noetherian base and does not repeat the constant-rank fallacy of FND-0131.

Hence V is locally free of rank 2, its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, and the canonical map p^*V -> omega_{C/T}(-Gamma) is identified with gamma^* of the canonical evaluation sigma^*sigma_*O_P(1) -> O_P(1) twisted by M^{-1}. The latter is surjective and exhibits P = P((sigma_*O_P(1))^vee); therefore p^*V -> omega_{C/T}(-Gamma) is surjective and the induced T-morphism

  g: C -> P(V^vee), g^*O(1) = omega_{C/T}(-Gamma),

satisfies: there is a unique isomorphism c: P -> P(V^vee) with g = c o gamma. Thus (P,gamma) is reconstructed from (C,Gamma) by a construction that uses only omega_{C/T}, Gamma and pushforward, hence is functorial in T and compatible with arbitrary base change (this is the point at which the recorded objection - fibrewise recovery does not control families, especially where p_*(omega(-Gamma)) changes rank - is met: the rank is proved constant with base change over arbitrary bases).

### 6.2 Full faithfulness and its consequences

Let Z, Z' be objects of Z(T) and let phi:(C,x_bullet) -> (C',x'_bullet) be an isomorphism in M_{6,6}(T). Then phi carries omega_{C/T} to omega_{C'/T} canonically and Gamma to Gamma', hence induces an isomorphism V -> V' and therefore an isomorphism psi: P -> P' with psi o gamma = gamma' o phi, by 6.1. Such a psi is unique because gamma is an epimorphism and P' is separated. Hence Hom_Z(Z,Z') -> Hom_{M_{6,6}}(Theta Z, Theta Z') is bijective: Theta is fully faithful on T-points for every T, i.e. a monomorphism of stacks. (This is proved on arbitrary families, not from injectivity on geometric points plus injectivity on automorphism groups.) Consequences:

- Theta is representable (a monomorphism of algebraic stacks is representable by algebraic spaces).
- Theta is unramified: a monomorphism has trivial relative diagonal, hence Omega = 0, and Theta is locally of finite type since Z and M_{6,6} are of finite type over k.
- Theta is quasi-finite: unramified plus finite type gives finite discrete fibres. This replaces the invalid route that mixed injectivity over one stratum with a fibre-dimension bound over another; here there is only one stratum (h^0 is constant by (3.2)) and quasi-finiteness comes from the monomorphism property, not from a dimension bound.
- Inertia: taking T = Spec of an algebraically closed field and Z = Z', the bijection of 6.2 gives Aut_Z(C,gamma,x_bullet) = Aut(C,x_bullet); the same argument applied to the unordered divisor gives Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) = Aut(C,Gamma). Note the direction: we start from an automorphism preserving the marked points and prove that it preserves the pencil (because it preserves omega_{C}(-Gamma), whose reconstruction returns gamma). No claim is made that these groups are trivial, and no PGL_2 fixed-point argument is used; the possibility that a nontrivial automorphism of a genus-6 curve fixes six points is irrelevant to the statement proved.
- Image and codimension: a quasi-finite morphism from a stack of pure dimension 17 has constructible image of pure dimension 17 (Chevalley plus finiteness of fibres), so the image has codimension 21-17 = 4 in M_{6,6}. Nothing is claimed about closedness, purity of the closure, or existence of a Gysin map.
- Local structure: an unramified morphism factors, etale-locally on the source, as a closed immersion followed by an etale morphism (standard local structure theorem, applied on smooth atlases of Z and M_{6,6}). Both Z and M_{6,6} are smooth over k of dimensions 17 and 21, and a closed immersion of smooth k-stacks is a regular immersion of codimension equal to the dimension difference. Hence etale-locally on Z, Theta is a regular closed immersion of codimension 4 into a stack etale over M_{6,6}. This is the valid route (a closed immersion between objects smooth over the base, codimension = dimension difference); no lci or Gysin conclusion is drawn from any comparison of actual with expected determinantal codimension.

## 7. Bridge to the Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure incidence

Assume (N): i^*O_X(1) iso omega_{C/P} tensor gamma^*A. Fibrewise deg(i^*O_X(1)) = 2g-2+8 = 18 = deg(omega_{C/P}) forces deg A = 0, so A has fibre degree zero on the genus-0 fibration and hence A = sigma^*(sigma_*A) is pulled back from the base. Let L_5 be the canonical maximal-degree line subbundle of the balanced F (ATT-0065/CLM-0065-5; it is unique because Hom(L_5,F/L_5) has fibrewise sections H^0(O(-1)) = 0, so the etale-local constructions glue), and W_5 := i^*O_X(2) tensor gamma^*L_5^vee, L := W_5 tensor omega_{C/T}^{-1}. Then

  L = omega_{C/T} tensor gamma^*(O_P(4) tensor A^2 tensor L_5^vee),

and O_P(4) tensor A^2 tensor L_5^vee has fibre degree 4+0-5 = -1, hence equals O_P(-1) tensor sigma^*(line bundle on T). Therefore L iso Lbar tensor pi^*M_0 for a line bundle M_0 on the base, and the Abel-Jacobi incidences for L and Lbar coincide (the incidence depends only on the class of the bundle modulo pullbacks from the base). By ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 (dual-confirmed by REV-0108, REV-0109) this incidence is exactly the balanced CE evaluation-failure scheme, and by ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6 its ordered distinct-support part is the S_6-torsor over Z_ev. Hence clauses (A)-(E) apply verbatim to the CE evaluation-failure locus under (N), while (A)-(E) themselves are proved for the canonical Lbar without (N).

Partial progress on the normalization itself (recorded, not used): for any finite flat degree-four cover gamma:C->P with C, P smooth, the natural map gamma^*E -> omega_{C/P} is surjective. Indeed gamma_*omega_{C/P} = Hom_{O_P}(gamma_*O_C,O_P) and E is the kernel of evaluation at 1. On a fibre, A is a finite Gorenstein k(y)-algebra of rank 4 with omega = A^vee cyclic; if A has several local factors, the projection of ker(ev_1) to each factor is onto, so ker(ev_1) generates; if A is local, A^vee = A.phi_0 with phi_0 a generator, ker(ev_1) corresponds to ker(phi_0), and ker(phi_0) contained in the maximal ideal m would force phi_0|_m = 0, contradicting nondegeneracy of the pairing (a,b) -> phi_0(ab); hence ker(ev_1) is not inside m.A^vee and generates by Nakayama. This gives a canonical P-morphism i_can with i_can^*O(1) = omega_{C/P}, so (N) holds whenever the CE embedding is the relative-canonical one; the identification of the CE embedding with i_can is not proved here and (N) remains an explicit hypothesis, in line with FND-0105.

## 8. Status separation

Proved here (unconditional, given (CE)): smoothness, finite type, Deligne-Mumford property and pure dimension 15 of Tet and of Bal; openness of balancedness; nonemptiness of Bal and of Z by the explicit complete intersection; h^0(D)=2, h^0(Lbar)=3, h^1(Lbar)=2 and the existence of a reduced member on every balanced fibre; local freeness and arbitrary base change of p_*Lbar over Bal and hence over arbitrary, possibly nonreduced, locally Noetherian bases and stack bases; the P^2-bundle model and its pure dimension 17; surjectivity and smoothness of I^dist->Bal; the S_6-torsor and the identification of connected with irreducible components; the component bijections and the [S_6:H_alpha] count; full faithfulness of Theta on all T-points, hence monomorphism, representability, unramifiedness, quasi-finiteness; the inertia isomorphisms; the constructible image of pure dimension 17 and codimension 4; the etale-local regular immersion of codimension 4; the surjectivity of gamma^*E -> omega_{C/P}.

Source-backed inputs (used, not proved here): SRC-0004 for the CE convention, the relative degree-four resolution and deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f; FND-0107 for the Abel-Jacobi/Hilbert incidence model; FND-0105 for the status of (N); the established working-context facts (i)-(iv) of Section 0; algebraicity of the moduli stacks of genus-0 fibrations and of finite flat algebras. Verified dependency artifacts: ATT-0065 with REV-0108/REV-0109; ATT-0066 with REV-0110/REV-0116; supporting context ATT-0086 with REV-0135/REV-0138 and ATT-0088 with REV-0139/REV-0142.

Computational hypotheses: none. The complete-intersection computation of Section 2.2 is a symbolic verification supporting existence statements only (Bal nonempty, Z nonempty); no universal claim rests on it.

Open gaps, unchanged by this artifact: the number of connected components of Bal (irreducibility of the balanced locus); the monodromy images H_alpha, in particular whether some H_alpha is transitive or contains a transposition; closedness or properness of Theta, the closure of its image and its absolute purity; the unbalanced CE strata and closure points outside Bal; whether a balanced cover can factor through a positive-genus intermediate curve; discharge of (N) itself; and all Hodge, weight, purity and Tate conclusions, which are downstream of this subproblem.

claims.justification: Section 1: boundedness of the splitting types of gamma_*O_C gives finite type; automorphism pairs are finite because the target automorphism is determined by the source one; deformations with fixed target are controlled by L_{C/P} = Omega_{C/P}, a torsion sheaf of length 2g-2+2d = 18, with Ext^2(Omega_{C/P},O_C)=0 and dim Ext^1 = 18; smooth surjective descent along Cov -> Tet of relative dimension 3 gives 18-3 = 15.
claims.statement: The stack Tet of triples (C,P,gamma) with C smooth proper of genus 6, P a genus-0 fibration and gamma finite flat of degree 4 is an algebraic Deligne-Mumford stack of finite type over k, smooth of pure dimension 15.

claims.justification: Section 2.1 computes h^0(F_b(-6)) = 4-a for F_b = O(a)+O(9-a) with a <= 4, so the vanishing is equivalent to a = 4, and semicontinuity gives openness; Section 2.2 exhibits a smooth (1,2)-(2,2) complete intersection in P^1 x P^2 with E=O(3)^3 and p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)) = O(4)+O(5); a nonempty open substack of a smooth pure-15-dimensional stack is smooth of pure dimension 15, and a connected normal locally Noetherian stack is irreducible.
claims.statement: Balancedness is the open condition h^0(F_b tensor omega_{P_b}^{tensor 3})=0, and the balanced locus Bal is nonempty; hence Bal is smooth of pure dimension 15, reduced and normal, and its irreducible components coincide with its connected components.

claims.justification: Section 3: Clifford applied to the special degree-4 bundle D, with the equality case excluded by the hyperelliptic-unbalanced fact; Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for Lbar; a double base point of |Lbar| would give a special g^2_4, hence Clifford equality, hence hyperellipticity, hence unbalanced relations, so the fixed part is reduced and Bertini applies to the base-point-free moving part. The reduced-member statement is also contained in the verified context artifact ATT-0088 (REV-0139, REV-0142) and is not claimed as new.
claims.statement: On every geometric point of Bal, h^0(O_C(D))=2, h^0(Lbar)=3, h^1(Lbar)=2 with Lbar=omega_C(-D), and |Lbar| contains a divisor with six distinct points.

claims.justification: Section 4.1: Bal is smooth hence reduced, h^0 is constant by CLM-0098-3, so Grauert applies on a smooth atlas and descends; surjectivity of the base-change map at every point upgrades this to arbitrary base change; the identification of the incidence with the projectivization is FND-0107 and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-4 on a constant-h^0 reduced base.
claims.statement: Over Bal, p_*Lbar is locally free of rank 3 with formation commuting with arbitrary base change, and the Abel-Jacobi incidence I is canonically the Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle P((p_*Lbar)^vee), smooth and proper of pure relative dimension 2 and pure dimension 17.

claims.justification: Section 4.2: the family is classified by a morphism to Bal, all data are pullbacks, Sym^6 and the relative Picard functor commute with base change, and p_*Lbar commutes with arbitrary base change by CLM-0098-4. Grauert is never applied over the possibly nonreduced base, so FND-0131 is bypassed rather than contradicted; the smooth-atlas descent remark demanded by FND-0127 is recorded.
claims.statement: For every family of balanced tetragonal triples satisfying (CE) over an arbitrary locally Noetherian k-scheme, reduced or not, and over every locally Noetherian algebraic k-stack with a smooth atlas, the incidence is the pullback of I along the classifying morphism and is again a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle with p_*Lbar locally free of rank 3.

claims.justification: Section 5: CLM-0098-3 gives fibrewise nonemptiness of the distinct-support open inside the irreducible fibre P^2; the torsor statement is the established stack-level fact with no one-sided reduction; smoothness of Bal makes I and Z normal, so connected components are irreducible components, which is exactly the normality hypothesis FND-0132 requires for the [S_6:H] count.
claims.statement: I^dist -> Bal is surjective and smooth with irreducible two-dimensional fibres; Z -> I^dist is a finite etale S_6-torsor; Z is smooth of pure dimension 17; components of I^dist, of I and of Bal correspond bijectively; and over a component Bal_alpha with monodromy image H_alpha the number of irreducible components of Z is exactly [S_6:H_alpha].

claims.justification: Section 6.1: omega_{C/T}(-Gamma) = gamma^*O_P(1) tensor pi^*M^{-1}; sigma_*O_P(1) is a rank-2 bundle with base change since R^1 vanishes fibrewise; sigma_*(E^vee tensor O_P(1)) = 0 because the corresponding two-term complex has fibrewise injective differential, i.e. constant maximal rank, which forces a local splitting even over nonreduced bases; the evaluation is then gamma^* of the canonical surjection defining P.
claims.statement: The pair (P,gamma) is reconstructed functorially in families from (C,Gamma) as the canonical morphism C -> P(V^vee) with V = p_*(omega_{C/T}(-Gamma)); V is locally free of rank 2 and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change.

claims.justification: Section 6.2: CLM-0098-7 makes the reconstruction functorial, so every isomorphism of the images lifts uniquely; monomorphisms of algebraic stacks are representable, have trivial relative diagonal hence are unramified when locally of finite type, and unramified plus finite type gives quasi-finite. The inertia statement is the T = field case and goes from an automorphism preserving the marked points to preservation of the pencil; no triviality of stabilizers is asserted.
claims.statement: Theta: Z -> M_{6,6} is fully faithful on T-points for every T, hence a representable monomorphism; it is unramified and quasi-finite; and it induces isomorphisms Aut(C,gamma,x_bullet) -> Aut(C,x_bullet) and Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) -> Aut(C,Gamma).

claims.justification: Section 6.2: quasi-finiteness makes the image dimension equal the source dimension 17 while dim M_{6,6} = 21; the local structure theorem for unramified morphisms plus smoothness of Z and M_{6,6} over k makes the local closed immersion regular of codimension equal to the dimension difference. No closedness, purity of closure, global immersion or Gysin morphism is asserted.
claims.statement: The image of Theta is a constructible substack of M_{6,6} of pure dimension 17, hence of codimension 4, and etale-locally on Z the morphism Theta factors as a regular closed immersion of codimension 4 followed by an etale morphism.

claims.justification: Section 7: the degree identity deg(i^*O_X(1)|_C) = 18 = deg(omega_{C/P}) forces the residual twist A to have fibre degree 0, hence to be pulled back from the base; the canonical maximal-degree subbundle L_5 of the balanced F is unique, so W_5 is well defined; the resulting bundle differs from Lbar by a pullback from the base, which does not change the Abel-Jacobi incidence.
claims.statement: Under the weak CE relative-canonical normalization (N), L = W_5 tensor omega_{C/T}^{-1} is isomorphic to Lbar tensor pi^*M_0; hence the incidence studied in CLM-0098-4 to CLM-0098-9 is exactly the balanced CE evaluation-failure incidence of ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-5, and clauses (A)-(E) apply to it.

claims.justification: Section 7: on each fibre the algebra A is finite Gorenstein of rank 4 with A^vee cyclic; the subspace ker(ev_1) generates A^vee, by surjectivity of the projections in the multi-factor case and by nondegeneracy of the pairing (a,b) -> phi_0(ab) in the local case, followed by Nakayama. The identification of the CE embedding with i_can is not proved, so (N) remains a hypothesis.
claims.statement: For every finite flat degree-four cover gamma: C -> P of smooth schemes with C a curve, the natural map gamma^*E -> omega_{C/P} is surjective, defining a canonical P-morphism i_can with i_can^*O(1) = omega_{C/P}; consequently (N) holds whenever the CE embedding coincides with i_can.

gap_markers: GAP-COMP-COMPONENTS: the number of connected (equivalently irreducible) components of the balanced base Bal is not determined; irreducibility is not inferred from irreducibility of any ambient Hurwitz space.

GAP-COMP-MONODROMY: the etale monodromy images H_alpha in S_6 of the ordered torsor are not determined; neither fullness nor the existence of a transposition is proved, so the component count [S_6:H_alpha] is stated as a formula, not a number.

GAP-COMP-NORMALIZATION: clause (F), i.e. the identification of the canonical Lbar with the CE residual bundle L, is conditional on the weak CE relative-canonical normalization (N) of FND-0105; CLM-0098-11 reduces (N) to the identification of the CE embedding with the canonical relative-canonical morphism but does not discharge it.

GAP-COMP-CLOSURE: closedness and properness of Theta, the closure of its image, absolute purity of that closure, and the unconstructed unbalanced CE strata and closure points outside Bal are not treated; in particular non-closedness is not claimed.
GAP-COMP-GYSIN: only an etale-local regular closed immersion of codimension 4 is proved; no global closed immersion, no lci statement for the pair (M_{6,6}, image), and no Gysin morphism.

GAP-COMP-NONPRIMITIVE: whether a balanced degree-four pencil can factor through a degree-two map to a positive-genus intermediate curve is untouched; the arguments here use only the exclusion of the hyperelliptic-composed case, which is all that h^0(D)=2 requires.
GAP-COMP-TATE: no Hodge, weight, purity or Tate conclusion is drawn; the local systems carried by the S_6-torsor are not analysed.
novelty_claims: Proves that the tetragonal stack at (g,d)=(6,4) is smooth Deligne-Mumford of pure dimension 15 by deformation theory of covers with fixed target (obstructions in Ext^2(Omega_{C/P},O_C)=0, tangent space of dimension equal to the length 18 of Omega_{C/P}), a route insensitive to ramification collisions, and transfers this to the balanced open, which is thereby reduced, normal and of pure dimension 15.

Removes the reducedness restriction on the P^2-bundle model without contradicting FND-0131: the model is proved on the smooth universal balanced base and transported to arbitrary, possibly nonreduced, locally Noetherian bases and to stack bases with a smooth atlas by arbitrary base change, with the descent remark demanded by FND-0127.

Supplies the normality hypothesis that FND-0132 requires, so that the connected-component count of the ordered finite etale S_6-torsor is a genuine irreducible-component count [S_6:H_alpha] over each component of the balanced base.

Constructs the forgetful 1-morphism from the balanced ordered model to M_{6,6} and proves it is fully faithful on all T-points, hence a representable monomorphism, hence unramified and quasi-finite, with inertia isomorphism Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) = Aut(C,Gamma); the key new input is that the reconstruction of gamma from (C,Gamma) is functorial in families because p_*(omega(-Gamma)) is a rank-2 bundle with arbitrary base change, the exact point flagged as unresolved.

Derives the codimension-4 statement for the image as a theorem (quasi-finite image of a pure-17-dimensional stack in a 21-dimensional one) rather than by promoting a source-dimension count, and records only the etale-local regular immersion of codimension 4, with no closedness, purity or Gysin claim.

Exhibits an explicit balanced witness: a smooth (1,2)-(2,2) complete intersection in P^1 x P^2 with E = O(3)^3, F = p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)) = O(4)+O(5), normalization holding with A = O, and Lbar = O_C(0,1) base-point-free, so the balanced locus and the ordered distinct-support model are nonempty.

proof_dependencies.role: Verified C66-GEO-Z dependency: CLM-0065-5 (canonical maximal-degree line subbundle of a fibrewise balanced F and the induced filtration) and CLM-0065-9 (balanced ambient CE failure scheme equals the relative incidence O_C(Gamma) iso W_5 tensor omega^{-1}), used in Section 7.
First independent confirmation of CLM-0065-1 through CLM-0065-9.
Second independent confirmation of CLM-0065-1 through CLM-0065-9, including the reading of relative isomorphism as triviality up to pullback from the base, which Section 7 uses.

Verified C66-GEO-H0 dependency: CLM-0066-4 (projective-bundle model on a reduced constant-h^0 stratum), CLM-0066-5 (Abel-Jacobi/Hilbert incidence as the correct global model), CLM-0066-6 (stack-level ordered distinct-support S_6-torsor), used in Sections 4, 5, 7.
First independent confirmation of CLM-0066-1 through CLM-0066-6.

Second independent confirmation of CLM-0066-1 through CLM-0066-6, including the load-bearing reducedness restriction on the projective-bundle model that Section 4 is designed to remove by base change from a smooth universal base.
Verified supporting context (C66-COMP-COMP): CLM-0086-1/2, emptiness of the h^0(L)=4 stratum on the balanced locus; the normalization-free analogue is reproved in Section 3.2.
First independent confirmation of CLM-0086-1 and CLM-0086-2.
Second independent confirmation of CLM-0086-1 and CLM-0086-2.

Verified supporting context (C66-COMP-RANK): non-hyperellipticity, h^0(L)=3 and nonemptiness of the reduced-support locus under (CE)+(BAL)+(N); Section 3.3 gives an independent normalization-free proof and claims no novelty for that statement.
First independent confirmation of CLM-0088-1 through CLM-0088-10.
Second independent confirmation of CLM-0088-1 through CLM-0088-10.

Casnati-Ekedahl convention W_f = (O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|_C, the relative degree-four resolution used to define F = p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)), and deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f with deg(O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C) = 2g-2+8 = 18 at g=6.
Status of the weak CE relative-canonical normalization (N): carried as an explicit hypothesis for clause (F) only, never relabelled as an established fact.
Abel-Jacobi/Hilbert incidence is the correct model over all of the base, whereas Proj(pi_*L) is correct only over constant-h^0 opens.

summary: Determines the component, dimension, stabilizer and finite-cover behaviour of the balanced tetragonal model at (g,n)=(6,6). Deformation theory of finite flat covers with fixed genus-0 target (obstructions in Ext^2(Omega_{C/P},O_C)=0, deformation space of dimension equal to the length 18 of Omega_{C/P}) proves that the tetragonal stack is smooth Deligne-Mumford of pure dimension 15; balancedness is open and is nonempty by an explicit (1,2)-(2,2) complete intersection in P^1 x P^2 whose relations bundle p_*(I_C(2)) is computed to be O(4)+O(5). Smoothness supplies exactly the reducedness and normality hypotheses that FND-0131 and FND-0132 flag as missing: the P^2-bundle model is proved over the smooth universal balanced base and then transported to arbitrary, possibly nonreduced, locally Noetherian bases and to stack bases by base change instead of by Grauert, and the pi_1-orbit count [S_6:H_alpha] becomes a legitimate irreducible-component count. Every balanced fibre carries a reduced member of |Lbar| (a double base point would give a g^2_4, hence hyperellipticity, hence unbalanced relations), so the ordered distinct-support model is fibrewise dense and has pure dimension 17. Finally the forgetful 1-morphism to M_{6,6} is constructed and proved fully faithful on all T-points, hence a representable monomorphism, hence unramified and quasi-finite, with inertia Aut(C,x)=Aut(C,gamma,x) and constructible image of pure dimension 17, i.e. codimension 4; the reconstruction of gamma from (C,Gamma) is functorial via P(p_*(omega(-Gamma))^vee), whose rank-2 base-change behaviour is proved over arbitrary bases.

theorem_scope.base: arbitrary locally Noetherian k-schemes and locally Noetherian algebraic k-stacks with a smooth atlas, k of characteristic zero; no reducedness hypothesis anywhere in (C)
theorem_scope.dependency_scope: ATT-0065 and ATT-0066 are used only for the CE filtration/Fitting identification and the Abel-Jacobi incidence model, within their dual-confirmed scope; ATT-0086 and ATT-0088 are used as verified supporting context for B_4 = empty and for the existence of reduced members
theorem_scope.exclusions: irreducibility of Bal (number of components), the monodromy images H_alpha, existence of a transposition in H_alpha, closedness or properness of Theta and the closure of its image, unbalanced CE strata and closure points outside Bal, global closed immersion, lci or Gysin statements for (M_{6,6}, image), triviality of stabilizers, whether balanced covers can factor through a positive-genus intermediate curve, and all Hodge, weight, purity and Tate conclusions
theorem_scope.generality: fibrewise balanced tetragonal Casnati-Ekedahl families of genus-6 curves; clauses (A)-(E) are unconditional given (CE); clause (F) alone is conditional on the weak CE relative-canonical normalization (N) of FND-0105
theorem_scope.normalization_role: (N) is used only in clause (F) to identify the canonical bundle Lbar=omega_{C/T}(-D) with the CE residual bundle L=W_5 tensor omega^{-1} up to a twist pulled back from the base; every geometric statement is proved for Lbar

theorem_statement: Let k be a field of characteristic zero. Let Tet be the k-stack whose objects over a k-scheme T are triples (pi:C->T, sigma:P->T, gamma:C->P) with pi smooth proper with geometrically connected genus-6 fibres, sigma smooth proper with geometrically connected genus-0 fibres, and gamma finite flat of degree 4, morphisms being pairs of T-isomorphisms compatible with gamma. For such a triple set E:=(coker(O_P->gamma_*O_C))^vee (locally free of rank 3, fibre degree 9), O_P(1):=det(E) tensor omega_{P/T}^{tensor 4} (fibre degree 1), D:=gamma^*O_P(1) (fibre degree 4) and Lbar:=omega_{C/T} tensor gamma^*O_P(-1) (fibre degree 6). Assume the relative Casnati-Ekedahl structure (CE) of SRC-0004: a closed P-embedding i:C->X:=P(E^vee) with p o i=gamma whose ideal has the relative resolution 0->O_X(-4) tensor p^*det(F)->O_X(-2) tensor p^*F->I_C->0, where F:=p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)) is locally free of rank 2 and fibre degree 9 and commutes with arbitrary base change. Let Bal be the locus of geometric points with H^0(P_b, F_b tensor omega_{P_b}^{tensor 3})=0, equivalently F_b iso O(4) direct-sum O(5) (balanced). Let I->Bal be the Abel-Jacobi incidence Sym^6(C/Bal) x_{Pic^6(C/Bal)} Bal taken over the class of Lbar, let I^dist be its distinct-support open, and let Z:=Conf_6(C/Bal) x_{Sym^6(C/Bal)} I be the ordered model. Then: (A) Tet is an algebraic Deligne-Mumford stack of finite type over k, smooth of pure dimension 15, and Bal is open in Tet and nonempty, hence smooth of pure dimension 15, hence reduced and normal, so its irreducible components are exactly its connected components (their number is finite and is not determined here). (B) Explicit witness: a smooth complete intersection C of divisors of bidegrees (1,2) and (2,2) in P^1 x P^2 with gamma=pr_1 is a k-point of Bal; for it E=O(3)^{direct-sum 3}, X=P^1 x P^2 with O_X(1)=O(3,1), F=O(4) direct-sum O(5), i^*O_X(1)=omega_{C/P^1}, Lbar=O_C(0,1) is base-point-free and its general member consists of 6 distinct points. (C) On Bal, h^0(O_{C_b}(D_b))=2, h^0(Lbar_b)=3 and h^1(Lbar_b)=2 for every geometric point b; p_*Lbar is locally free of rank 3 and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change; I is canonically P((p_*Lbar)^vee), a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle, smooth and proper over Bal of pure relative dimension 2 and pure dimension 17. Consequently, for every family of triples satisfying (CE) and fibrewise balancedness over an arbitrary locally Noetherian k-scheme T, reduced or not, and over every locally Noetherian algebraic k-stack with a smooth atlas, the corresponding incidence is canonically I x_{Bal} T, again a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle with p_{T*}Lbar_T locally free of rank 3; no reducedness hypothesis is needed and Grauert is not applied over the possibly nonreduced base. (D) For every geometric point b of Bal the linear system |Lbar_b| contains a divisor with six distinct points, so I^dist->Bal is surjective and smooth with irreducible two-dimensional fibres; Z->I^dist is a finite etale S_6-torsor; Z is smooth of pure dimension 17; on Bal, I, I^dist and Z irreducible components coincide with connected components; the induced maps {components of I^dist}->{components of I}->{components of Bal} are bijections; and for each component Bal_alpha with etale monodromy image H_alpha in S_6 of the torsor over I^dist_alpha, the number of irreducible components of Z over Bal_alpha is exactly [S_6:H_alpha] (the subgroups H_alpha are not determined here). (E) The forgetful assignment Theta:Z->M_{6,6}, (C,P,gamma,x_1,...,x_6) |-> (C,x_1,...,x_6), is a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks which is fully faithful on T-points for every k-scheme T, hence a representable monomorphism; it is unramified and quasi-finite; for every object of Z it induces isomorphisms of inertia Aut(C,gamma,x_bullet) -> Aut(C,x_bullet) and Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) -> Aut(C,Gamma), because (P,gamma) is reconstructed functorially from (C,Gamma) as the canonical morphism to P((p_*(omega_{C/T}(-Gamma)))^vee); the image of Theta is a constructible substack of pure dimension 17, that is of codimension 4 in the 21-dimensional M_{6,6}; and etale-locally on Z the morphism Theta factors as a regular closed immersion of codimension 4 followed by an etale morphism to M_{6,6}. No global closed immersion, no properness, no closedness of the image and no Gysin morphism for the pair (M_{6,6}, image) is asserted. (F) Bridge to the Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure locus: under the weak CE relative-canonical normalization (N) that i^*O_X(1) iso omega_{C/P} tensor gamma^*A for some line bundle A on P, one has A of fibre degree 0, and with L:=W_5 tensor omega_{C/T}^{-1} for the canonical maximal-degree line subbundle L_5 of F and W_5:=i^*O_X(2) tensor gamma^*L_5^vee, one has L iso Lbar tensor pi^*M_0 for a line bundle M_0 on the base; hence I is exactly the balanced CE evaluation-failure incidence O_C(Gamma) iso L of ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-5, and clauses (A)-(E) apply verbatim to it. Clauses (A)-(E) themselves do not use (N).
